paragraphs: R' Menahama (one of the Palestinian amoraim of aggadah).
He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat ch. 14, halakhah 3: Rabbi Tanhuma in the name of Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Menahama in the name of Rav — all illness is bile.

Likewise we find in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 32, par. 2: Rabbi Tanhuma in the name of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Simon, Rabbi Menahama in the name of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose, said: no one loves his fellow tradesman, but the sage loves his fellow tradesman.
Likewise we find that he spoke in the name of R' Hiyya the Great, in Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 'Yehuda' [Hebrew: פ׳ יהודה], at the supplied locator ס״ד.

He also spoke in the name of R' Avin, as in Midrash Shmuel ch. 5, par. 16, and in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 105 and 144 (edition/page convention unresolved), and in Midrash Tehillim ch. 80, par. 2: R' Menahamya in the name of R' Avin.
And in Ruth Rabbah ch. 2, par. 4, in the name of R' Aha.
And in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 50, par. 7, ch. 80, par. 4, and Pesikta Rabbati, chapters Shekalim and Lifkudeihem, in the name of R' Bibi.
And in Tanhuma Aharei, par. 7: R' Menahama in the name of R' Yehoshua son of Hanina (Hyman says it should read 'son of Nehemiah,' as in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 172b).
And in Ruth Rabbah ch. 3, par. 6, in the name of R' Yehoshua son of Avin.

And in Midrash Shmuel ch. 15, par. 1, together with R' Nahman, in the name of R' Ya'akov of Caesarea; and there at the end of ch. 15, in the name of R' Mana; and there ch. 8, par. 2, in the name of R' Shmuel son of Rav Yitzhak.
We also find R' Hiyya son of Menahama in Vayikra Rabbah ch. 36, par. 6, and R' Yehoshua son of Menahama in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 53, par. 10.

Those are local expansions, not a global rule for the initials. The whole consulted Pesikta Rabbati 11, beginning “Yehuda and Israel,” includes the literal chain אמר ר׳ מנחמא בי ר׳ חייא הגדול בשם רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, alongside Hyman’s statement that Menachama spoke in the name of Chiyya the Great. The wording בי and the additional teacher are disclosed without silently changing Hyman’s chain or admitting a father identity. The supplied ס״ד is retained literally; this comparison does not establish the exact section/page conventions of Hyman’s printing, nor the other Pesikta de-Rav Kahana locators 105, 144 and 172b. Midrash Shmuel 5:16 directly has Menachama in the name of Avin, but the whole consulted Midrash Tehillim 80:2 gives Tanchuma in the name of Avin, beside Hyman’s Menachamya. These readings are not silently harmonized. Hyman’s definite Hanina-to-Nechemiah correction remains expressly his proposal; the actual returned Tanchuma Achrei Mot 7 concerns a different passage and is not treated as proof of that correction or of absence elsewhere. The final two patronymic notices are not proof that both men were sons of this particular Menachama. Other uncollated editions and locators remain attributed to Hyman. All Hebrew and current notes remain unchanged.
